'''''Magnolia figo''''' is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Magnoliaceae]].<ref name=POWO>{{cite web |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:554702-1 |title=''Magnolia figo'' (Lour.) DC. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=The Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=13 July 2025}}</ref><ref name=COL>{{cite web |url=https://www.catalogueoflife.org/data/taxon/3XH9V |title=Magnolia figo (Lour.) DC. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Catalogue of Life |publisher=Species 2000 |access-date=13 July 2025}}</ref> This [[evergreen]] tree is sometimes referred to by the common names '''banana shrub''', and '''port wine magnolia'''. It grows to {{convert|3-4|m|ft|abbr=off|0}} tall. 

Initially described by [[Portuguese people|Portuguese]] [[missionary]] and [[Natural history|naturalist]] [[João de Loureiro]] as ''[[Liriodendron]] figo'', it was reclassified as ''Michelia figo'' by German [[Botany|botanist]] [[Curt Polycarp Joachim Sprengel]]. In 2006, a [[Cladistics|cladistic]] analysis of the [[genus]] ''[[Michelia]]'' found them to lie within the genus ''[[Magnolia]]'', with the name now being ''Magnolia figo''.

It is cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]] in gardens for its fragrant flowers, which are cream-white and sometimes yellow, purple rounded, or light-purple, and strongly scented with [[isoamyl alcohol]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Knudsen |first1=Jeite T. |last2=Tollsten |first2=Lars |last3=Bergstrom |first3=L. Gunnar |title=Floral Scents - A Checklist of Volatile Compounds Isolated by Head-Space Techniques |journal=Phytochemistry |date=1993 |volume=33 |issue=2 |pages=253–280 |doi=10.1016/0031-9422(93)85502-i}}</ref> It is also popular to keep ''M. figo'' as a [[houseplant]]. [[Bud|Flower buds]], as well as new [[Leaf|leaves]], are covered with hairs, giving it a texture similar to that of [[velvet]]. The leaves are leathery, dark glossy-green, up to 10 cm long.

This plant is used in Shanghai, China, as a tall evergreen [[hedge]].  It grows very slowly and matures into a large [[evergreen]] compact tree.  It grows in acid and alkaline soil very well, but is susceptible to black soot.

==Distribution==
It is native to China.
